title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 28
paragraphs: Astonished at this last statement, Xerxes himself then asked Pythius how much money he had. Pythius answered: “O king, I will not hide the truth from you, nor will I excuse myself by saying that I do not know my own wealth, but I will tell it to you precisely, since I know. As soon as I heard that you were coming down to the Sea of Greece, wishing to give you money for the war, I ascertained the true figures, and reckoning I found that I had two thousand talents of silver, and in gold four million darics less seven thousand. This money I now present to you. For myself, I have enough to live on from my slaves and my estates.”
